one_month_reasoning: Window to 2026-11-08. (1) Q3 2026 results: not yet announced. Generac reported Q3 2025 on Oct 29 after a mid-October notice [17], and third-party calendars estimate Nov 4, so the print is very likely inside the window. Expect strong C&I and data-center commentary, including the first framing of 2027 with Amazon's $2.4B 2027-28 deliveries, which the 8-K calls 'expected' [4]; Amazon is the second hyperscaler (press report [6]; inference: Ex. 10.1 recites a Global Purchase Agreement with Amazon Data Services dated June 24, 2026, the date the Q2 release gives for the second hyperscale agreement; no filing or call names Amazon as the second hyperscaler [51]), so no extra hyperscale award should be expected. Residential should be soft after the quiet season [2][15]. Year-on-year comparisons will be messy after the Q2 refund. The 2027 framing and C&I margin can move the stock 10%+ either way, and I have no directional edge. (2) Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin late on Oct 9 with 105 mph winds and outages from Pensacola to Tallahassee [16]. It was forecast days ahead [15], so most of it is priced: a small positive. (3) Hyperscaler and Caterpillar/Cummins Q3 reports give read-through. I keep a near-symmetric lognormal with median $226, a hair above spot, and log-sd 16.5%, slightly above annual vol / 3.5 (56% / 3.5 = 16%) because earnings fall in the window. Unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of a segment SOTP on CY2027E EBITDA ($276.8: residential $669M x 12x + C&I $536M x 18x, less $1.064B net debt, 60.0M shares) and P/E on horizon NTM EPS ($239.2: $14.23 x 16.8x). (276.8 + 239.2) / 2 = $258.0, rounded to $258 (basis: estimate).

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Residential CY27E $2.68B x 25% = $669M x 12x = $8.03B; C&I CY27E $3.83B x 14% = $536M x 18x = $9.64B; EV $17.68B - net debt $1.064B = $16.61B / 60.0M = $276.8. At the Oct-2027 horizon trailing EBITDA approximates CY2027, so TTM peer multiples are applied.

H2 = $4.93B - H1 external $2.23B = $2.70B. Residential guided to high-single-digit growth and C&I to low-30s% growth [1]; data-center revenue 'nearly $450 million' in 2026 [2]. Split H2 ~$1.38B residential / ~$1.31B C&I.

$1.35B of backlog 'scheduled for deliveries in 2027' [2] (the $1.6B backlog excludes the second hyperscaler) + ~$0.45B (about 19%) of Amazon's $2.4B 2027-28 initial deliveries [4]. Amazon is the second hyperscaler (press report [6]; inference: Ex. 10.1 recites a Global Purchase Agreement with Amazon Data Services dated June 24, 2026, the date the Q2 release gives for the second hyperscale agreement; no filing or call names Amazon as the second hyperscaler [51]), so the $2.4B is incremental to the backlog and there is no further second-hyperscaler award. Amazon is weighted to 2028 because capacity is >$1.25B/yr by Q4 2026 and reaches ~3x only by end-Q3 2027 [13].

FY26E $2.55B x 1.05. Outages >30% below baseline in Q2 [2], a quiet 2026 season until Isaias [15][16], and US residential solar weakness after the 25D credit expired [14] (the source shows storage shipments rising, not weakness) cap growth; dealer network ~9,700 and still growing [2]; assumes a normal 2027 outage year.
Non-data-center C&I $2.38B - $0.45B = $1.93B x 1.05 = $2.03B, plus data center $1.80B = $3.83B. Total CY27E $2.68B + $3.83B = $6.50B, equal to the $6.50B consensus [7].
Equal to the H1 2026 ex-refund 25.4% (rounded down), on the assumption that the refund does not recur and higher tariffs offset part of the recovery [2].

Ex-refund H1 2026 was 12.8%. +1.2 pts for operating leverage on +61% C&I sales and firmer large-genset pricing ($450-600/kW installed vs $380-420/kW in 2023 [12]), tempered by hyperscale margins being 'lower than that of our non-hyperscale customers' [2] and ramp costs. Still far below Cummins Power Systems at 24.5% [9]. Implied CY27 consolidated margin: $1,205M / $6.50B = 18.5%, at the bottom of the FY26 underlying 18.5-19.5% guide [1].

bear.story: Data-center ramp disappoints or AI capex digests. Amazon (Firm Orders of a redacted minimum [51]; the 8-K gives no amount [4]) and the first hyperscaler slow 2028 call-offs as CAT, Cummins, Rehlko and Generac all add capacity, so large-genset pricing rolls over. Residential stays soft with another quiet storm year, and without the ~$0.90 2026 tariff refund the +48% underlying FY27 growth in consensus is missed. FY28 EPS ~$10.5-11 at ~14x.

base.story: Data-center revenue goes from ~$450M to ~$1.8B in 2027 ($1.35B of scheduled backlog + ~$0.45B of Amazon) and ~$2-2.6B in 2028. C&I underlying margin rises from ~12.8% to ~14%; residential grows ~5% at ~25% margin. EPS tracks consensus ($12.97 FY27), and the stock trades ~17x horizon NTM EPS of ~$14.2, a segment-mix discount to the 24.8-27.8x peer medians.

bull.story: Large-genset shortages persist through 2028 (18-24 month lead times [12]). GNRC fills its tripled capacity, Amazon purchases move well beyond the initial $2.4B toward the $8B ceiling, the first hyperscaler re-orders, and an active 2027 hurricane season revives home standby. FY28 EPS ~$16.5 at ~21x. No separate second-hyperscaler award is assumed: that customer is Amazon (inference from the Ex. 10.1 June 24 date match; press [6]).

reasoning: Round 2 changes, driven by the supervisor. (1) FY27 consensus EPS is now $12.97 (StockAnalysis/S&P Global, reopened; FY27 revenue $6.50B) in place of the keyed $12.67. (2) I re-derived segment margins from the Q2 release: the tariff refund took ~9 pts off residential and ~2 pts off C&I segment margins, so H1 ex-refund margins are 25.4% residential and 12.8% C&I (13.9% reported). I cut CY27 C&I margin from 15% to 14%. (3) I resolved the second-hyperscaler question. The Q2 release says a second hyperscale agreement was secured June 24 (the first was signed earlier in Q2, ~$700M committed for 2027), final 2027-28 terms were still in negotiation, and its volumes are excluded from the $1.6B backlog. The Amazon 8-K (Sept 16) gives $2.4B of initial 2027-28 deliveries, and The Daily Upside reports the filing revealed the second deal was with Amazon. Amazon is therefore, by inference (press [6] plus the Ex. 10.1 June 24 recital [51]; no filing states it), the second hyperscaler: the $2.4B is incremental to the backlog, and I removed the separate second-hyperscaler catalyst and bull upside. (4) The $725B hyperscaler-capex roundup, the Alphabet 2027 comment, the dealer podcast, Q3 consensus/revision counts and the $173 trough no longer feed any number; I dropped them. (5) Multiples: the supervisor asked why C&I gets 18x vs the 20.1x CMI/CAT TTM mean. 18x is below that mean, and I keep it as a ~10% discount for new-entrant status, customer concentration, the warrant price concession and capacity risk. I also re-anchored the C&I P/E from the electrical cluster (24x) to the direct genset competitors (19.7x), which lowers the P/E leg. Industry evidence is unchanged and was reopened where it drives numbers: Cummins Power Systems +19% with a 24.5% EBITDA margin on data-center standby demand [9]; Caterpillar power-gen strength and capacity adds [10]; large-genset lead times of 18-24 months and higher $/kW pricing [12]; Generac at >$1.25B/yr large-MW capacity by Q4 2026, ~3x by end-Q3 2027 [13]; residential softness [2][14][15]. Valuation: SOTP $276.8, P/E $239.2, fair value $258 (from $270). Ladder: three lognormal scenarios. Bear $150 (25%, log-sd 0.35), base $245 (50%, 0.28), bull $350 (25%, 0.28). Mean ~$258, median ~$244, P(>= $225) 0.58, overall log-sd ~0.43. That is below the brief's 56% realized volatility (jump-inflated by the Amazon deal day) but keeps fat tails (1.8% below $90, 1.2% above $562). Research limits: sec.gov refused scripted access, so filings were read via WebFetch; Nasdaq returned 503; no keyed API data, option prices or implied volatility were used.
